viewsWelcome.contents:
No data collected yet.
A scan reads each configured MCP server's tool definitions and measures what they cost per session.
[Scan now](command:mcp-lens.scanNow)
To see actual usage, install the collection hooks from the Setup Status view.
[Open Setup Status](command:mcpLens.setupStatus.focus)

mcpLens.reportDays.markdownDescription: Number of days the status bar summary and reports aggregate over. Original client logs expire after about 30 days, but the Lens DB retains data permanently, so longer periods can also be queried.

enumDescriptions: Summarizes with a focus on the action list. Candidate and normal tool lists show only the top 5 (default)
mcpLens.reportDetail.markdownDescription: Detail level for `MCP Lens: Show Report`. Items needing action and items to inspect are always shown in full regardless of this setting.

enumDescriptions: Asks with a notification popup when a new server to scan is detected
Scans a newly detected server right away, without asking. The very first scan is still left to you: nothing is scanned automatically until you have scanned once from the walkthrough
Never scans on its own (default until you opt in during onboarding). Scan from the walkthrough, the matrix view, or the MCP Lens: Scan MCP Servers command
mcpLens.autoScan.markdownDescription: Automatic scanning of MCP server tool definitions. Scanning briefly runs each registered stdio server and requests tools/list. No LLM tokens are spent and no config file is modified.

mcpLens.authIgnore.markdownDescription: MCP server names for which the sign-in-required notification will not be shown again. Automatically added via the `Don't ask for this server` button.

mcpLens.oauthClients.markdownDescription: OAuth client ids for MCP servers that refuse automatic (dynamic) client registration, such as GitHub's and Figma's remote servers: `{ "github": "Iv1.abc123" }`. Register an OAuth app with the provider and paste its client id. A client secret is never stored here; sign in from the Setup Status view and it is written to `~/.mcplens/oauth/clients.json` with owner-only permissions, where the `mcp-lens` CLI reads it too.

mcpLens.unsupportedServers.markdownDescription: MCP server names that Lens has determined it does not support (for example, servers that reject automatic client registration). Automatically added during a sign-in attempt; these servers are hidden from the tree and never prompted for sign-in again.

mcpLens.inferenceProvider.markdownDescription: Provider used for dependency analysis. With `auto`, automatic analysis picks Claude when both CLIs are installed; set this explicitly to pin one.

mcpLens.autoAnalyze.markdownDescription: After a server is scanned automatically, analyze its new tools to judge whether each one can be turned off independently. **This calls the provider CLI (Claude or Codex) and spends its tokens**, and it sends tool definitions and aggregated usage counts to that provider. It reuses the consent you already gave and never runs before you have consented once, so the first analysis is always yours to start from the walkthrough. Only tools that have not been analyzed before are sent.

mcpLens.claudeModel.markdownDescription: Claude model used for dependency analysis.

mcpLens.codexModel.markdownDescription: Codex model used for dependency analysis.

enumDescriptions: Global actions are locked. Lens never edits your client config.
Allow global actions for Claude Code only.
Allow global actions for Codex only.
Allow global actions for Claude Code and Codex.
mcplens.dependencyAnalysis.rollout.markdownDescription: Controls which client is allowed to use global actions (disabling an unused MCP tool by editing that client's config file). Analysis, cache, and details remain available for every value, including `off`. Gemini CLI is not supported by global actions and is never allowed.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with MCP Lens
walkthroughs.description: Measure what your MCP tools cost, then decide what to turn off.

steps.title: Scan your MCP servers
steps.description:
Measure how many tokens each tool definition costs in every prompt. Lens briefly starts each configured server and calls tools/list. No LLM tokens are spent and no config file is modified.
[Scan now](command:mcp-lens.scanNow)

steps.title: Turn on usage collection
steps.description:
Install hooks into your AI coding clients. Hooks record how often each tool is actually called, which is what definition cost is compared against.
Codex also needs you to approve the hooks under /hooks. Gemini CLI needs a restart. Either way, collection starts with your next session.
Setup Status in the sidebar always shows the live state.
[Install hooks](command:mcp-lens.installHooksAll)

steps.title: Analyze tool dependencies
steps.description:
Find out which tools you can turn off without breaking others. This calls your Claude or Codex CLI and spends that account's tokens, so you pick the provider and confirm the cost here first. Only tool definitions and aggregated usage counts are sent; prompts, tool inputs, tool outputs and source code are never sent. Afterwards, servers you add later are analyzed automatically with the same choice (turn that off with mcpLens.autoAnalyze).
[Analyze now](command:mcplens.analyzeDependencies)

steps.title: Finish setup: automation and global actions
steps.description:
Decide whether Lens keeps itself up to date when you add a new MCP server later, then choose whether it may turn unused tools off for you by editing your client config. Both are off until you say otherwise.
[Finish setup](command:mcp-lens.openRolloutSetting)
